newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods to knock down Polish PZU insurer's price.
newsitem.headline: Floods to knock down Polish PZU insurer's price.

text.p: Large-scale pay-outs for flood damages will diminish the attractiveness of Poland's biggest insurer PZU SA ahead of its planned privatisation next year, the company's spokesman said on Friday.

Marek Maszek told Reuters most of the pay-outs were not reinsured, because in December PZU started reinsuring only claims on flats and objects worth more than $500,000 as a part of a cost cutting scheme.
The state-owned PZU announced it will have to pay damages amounting to 568 million zlotys.
"It is very likely that the damages would have been lower ... These amounts may weaken our position in the (privatization) negotiations," Maszek said.

"We concentrated on reinsuring large-risk entities, where one-off damages could be very serious, and we limited the reinsurance in the case of less risky policies, such as flat insurance," Maszek said.
Under PZU's privatization programme the firm was to sell up to 49 percent of its shares to raise 600 million zlotys for current needs by July 31, Maszek said. But the floods delayed all decisions. @
"The Council of Ministers did not make a decision on the sale of the shares, partly due to the flooding," Maszek said.
Among 21 companies intending to become PZU's stable investors are Peako SA bank and computer firm Prokom. PZU plans to enter the Warsaw bourse.
